package_info.package_versions: All published versions (auto-generated, no specific versioning mentioned)
package_info.why_malicious: These packages are malicious because they are mass-produced with the sole purpose of luring users to phishing websites via links embedded in their README.md files. The packages do not provide legitimate software functionality and are designed to facilitate phishing, credential harvesting, and referral fraud.

execution_context.trigger: import-time (package discovery, npmjs.com browsing, or npm install readme rendering)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When a user views the package README (either on npmjs.com, in a code editor, or after installation), the README displays a link that redirects through a URL shortener to a phishing website, leading to further redirects and ultimately to eCommerce sites with referral IDs.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: README files in legitimate packages typically provide documentation, not links to external, unrelated download sites, especially via URL shorteners.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal package READMEs describe usage, API, or installation instructions. Here, the README is weaponized to lure users to phishing and scam sites.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages may link to official documentation or demo sites, but not to unrelated eBook downloads or through obfuscated shorteners.
key_indicators: Use of URL shorteners (tinybit.cc) to hide destination
Mass creation of packages with similar README content
Phishing and referral scam destination domains

attack_chain.action: Attacker creates thousands of npm packages with auto-generated names and similar README.md files containing phishing links.
attack_chain.leads_to: Users discover or install the package and view the README.

attack_chain.action: User views the README, sees the enticing eBook download link, and clicks it.
attack_chain.leads_to: User is redirected via a URL shortener to a phishing site.

attack_chain.action: Phishing site presents fake eBook download, captcha, and further redirects.
attack_chain.leads_to: User is subjected to additional phishing, adware, and referral scam sites.

attack_chain.action: Final redirect leads to eCommerce sites with attacker's referral ID, generating financial rewards for the attacker.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker profits from referral rewards; user may be phished or scammed.

behavioral_signatures: README.md files containing links to unrelated external sites, especially via URL shorteners
Mass publication of packages with similar or identical README content
Packages with no functional code, only documentation spam
file_indicators: README.md containing [tinybit.cc] or other URL shortener links
README.md with eBook download offers or unrelated promotional content
network_indicators: Redirects to pdflivres.com and other known phishing domains
Final redirects to eCommerce sites with suspicious referral IDs
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor newly published npm packages for README.md files containing links to URL shorteners or unrelated external domains. Flag packages with no functional code and similar auto-generated metadata. Analyze referral IDs and destination domains for known phishing or scam activity. Automated scanning of README content for suspicious patterns can help identify such campaigns.
